> `obs_count` is **not comparable across runs** — most fetchers report rows merged this run, thirteen fall back to the whole store when nothing was written. To ask how big this source is, count the store. See ledger R326 and the comment in `updater/state.py`.

> A `partial` NEVER sets `last_success_utc` (R231). A source reading `last SUCCESS: NEVER` may be ingesting millions of rows perfectly well and failing one sub-unit. Check `obs_count` and the run history before concluding it is dead.

> **A FUTURE `last_obs_date` IS USUALLY CORRECT, NOT A BUG.** Many publishers ship genuine PROJECTIONS: CSO Ireland's `18_Population_Projections` runs to 2057, Estonia's `rahvastik` to 2085, ABS to 2046/2071, UN WPP to 2101, IMF WEO to 2031. `health.py` already separates the two — `frontier` is the furthest period held INCLUDING projections (display only), `newest_obs` filters to periods <= today and is the recency signal — because 28 of 93 units legitimately reported a future frontier. Do NOT "repair" a future date until you have looked at the series key and the year sequence.
>
> What IS a defect: a SENTINEL (9999-12-31, 2999-12-31) or a COUNTER read as a year (years 1, 2, 3 ... contiguous from 1 — no projection starts at year 1). Tell them apart by the key and the sequence, never by the size of the number. See R320/R322 and `tools/audit_impossible_dates.py`, whose bounds (before 1500, after 2200) are deliberately far outside every real projection horizon.

## 3. How it works

**Why this strategy** (registry `strategy_reason`):

> The rplumber bulk endpoint returns the WHOLE indicator table with no since/start param, so the change signal has to come from the TOC. CORRECTED 2026-07-30 - this entry proposed gating on n.records GROWTH, which is strictly weaker than what ILO already publishes. A revision that rewrites values without changing the row count is invisible to a count gate, and so is a correction that SHRINKS it. The TOC's own last.update stamp is populated for 1,956 of 1,956 indicators, so the fetcher gates on that instead.

**Adapter contract** (registry `adapter`):

- `vintage_signal`: Re-download TOC data/raw/ilostat/toc_indicator_en.csv (rplumber.ilo.org); per id compare TOC n.records against manifest 'rows'/'expected'; if TOC count exceeds recorded rows, re-pull that id's full parquet and overwrite atomically.
- `since_param`: n/a
- `out_paths_note`: Multi-file: ~1947 per-indicator-frequency parquets at data/clean_full/ilostat/<id>.parquet, plus run state data/raw/ilostat/_manifest.csv and TOC data/raw/ilostat/toc_indicator_en.csv (single output dir).
- `rate_note`: No key (rplumber.ilo.org bulk API). Concurrency capped at 6 workers; per-request timeout 900s; 5-retry exp backoff honoring 429; validates payload begins b'PAR1'.

**Fetcher module**: [`updater/strategies/fetchers/ilostat.py`](../../updater/strategies/fetchers/ilostat.py)

<details><summary>Its own module docstring — the authoritative description, including every defect previously found and why the code looks the way it does</summary>

```
S1 bulk fetcher — ILOSTAT indicators (rplumber.ilo.org, no key).

ILO publishes 1,947 indicators, one parquet each, plus a table-of-contents CSV describing
every one of them.

THE VINTAGE IS PUBLISHER-SUPPLIED, WHICH IS THE BEST CASE. The TOC carries a `last.update`
timestamp per indicator (e.g. '27/05/2026 10:13:03') and it is populated for 1,947 of 1,947
rows. That beats every HTTP-validator scheme in this tree: it is ILO's own statement of when
each dataset changed, so there is nothing to infer and nothing that can flap. It sidesteps the
defect class that bit fed_board (Last-Modified regenerated per request) and bis (ETags flapping
across replicas) — there is no header to be wrong about.

THE TOC MUST BE RE-DOWNLOADED, NOT READ FROM CACHE. `ig.read_toc()` uses the file on disk when
one exists and only downloads if it is missing. On a schedule that is a staleness bomb of the
exact stats_nz shape (R159): the gate would compare every indicator against a frozen snapshot
of last.update and conclude, forever, that nothing had changed. So `ig.download_toc()` is
called first, explicitly, every run.

COST. One TOC download per run, then a fetch ONLY for indicators whose last.update moved.
Steady state is therefore one small CSV. The FIRST run is different and deliberately so: the
sidecar starts empty, so every indicator reads as changed and the wall-clock budget defers most
of them to later runs. That is honest — the alternative, seeding the sidecar from the current
TOC because 1,947 parquets happen to already be on disk, would ASSERT those files match ILO's
current last.update without ever checking, which is how a source ends up frozen and green.

PARSING AND WRITING ARE REUSED from jobs.ingest_ilostat (`process_one` -> build_table ->
parquet), so the fetcher and the first-pass ingest cannot drift. `process_one` writes locally
with pq.write_table and ig.OUT is the same directory as config.source_dir, so the bytes are
already at their store path and blob.publish_file streams them to R2 (only blob knows about
R2 — R36).

HONEST-STATUS: TOC unreachable -> TransientError (partial, retried, data kept). A per-indicator
failure -> transient_unit for that indicator only, so one bad download cannot stop the other
1,946. An indicator that returns ZERO rows while the TOC says it has records -> structural_unit
with its last.update NOT recorded, so it resurfaces next run; an indicator the TOC itself
declares empty (n.records = 0) is NOT an error and is counted as unchanged.
```

</details>

**Ingest script(s)**: `jobs/ingest_ilostat.py`

## 4. If it stops updating — diagnose in this order

Run everything from `E:\research\econfindatalibrary`.

```bash
# 1. What does the system actually say? (not what you remember)
python -c "import sys,sqlite3;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config;con=sqlite3.connect(f'file:{config.STATE_DB}?mode=ro',uri=True);print(*con.execute(\"SELECT unit_id,status,last_success_utc,last_attempt_utc,last_error FROM unit_state WHERE source_id='ilostat'\"),sep=chr(10))"

# 2. Is it even being ATTEMPTED? 'scheduled' is not 'attempted' (R246).
#    A daily run reaches ~20 of ~106 cloud sources; most are skipped on cadence, which is normal.
python -m updater.run --source ilostat --dry

# 3. Run it for real and READ THE REASON. Failures name themselves now.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -u -m updater.run --source ilostat --force

# 4. Is the PUBLISHER healthy, or is it us? Probe upstream directly, never a relay.
#    (DBnomics is BANNED — every source must be reached at its own publisher.)

# 5. Is the store intact? obs_count in state is NOT the answer.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -c "import sys,os;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config,blob;d=config.source_dir('ilostat');fs=[f for f in blob.list_parquets(d) if not os.path.basename(f).startswith('_')];print(len(fs),'files',sum(blob.row_count(os.path.join(d,os.path.basename(f))) for f in fs),'rows')"

# 6. Are its dates real? A counter-as-year or a 9999 sentinel is silent (7 sources hit).
#    NOTE: a FUTURE date is usually a legitimate projection - check the key before repairing.
python tools/audit_impossible_dates.py --r2 --source ilostat
```

**Read the failure class before fixing anything.** From the 2026-08-04 audit of every unfetchable source, the causes were: `budget_deferral` (NOT broken — ran out of its time slice), `code_bug`, `rate_limited`, `gated_by_design`. **Zero** were an expired credential or a dead endpoint, although that is the usual first guess.

If the error names sub-units as `deferred (budget N min)` or `budget spent`, **nothing has failed** — the source ran out of its slice and the rest is taken next tick (R303). Do not 'fix' it.

## 4b. Root cause when this was last investigated (2026-08-04)

*From the unfetchable-source audit — 29 agents, every finding challenged by a skeptic before it was accepted. This source was covered by the target `ilostat`.*

- **root cause**: `budget_deferral`  (confidence high)
- **which units**: Zero units failed. 675 of 1,956 were attempted and all 675 succeeded; the other 1,281 were never attempted — the 25-minute Deadline stopped the sweep at sorted index 675 and the pre-2026-08-03 code counted those untouched units through transient_unit(), so they were reported as failures and also inflated the `attempted` denominator. Under the current code the same run reports "675 sub-unit(s) attempted, none failed; 1281 deferred by budget and taken next tick".
- **blast radius**: No data loss and no broken endpoint — 126,799,245 rows were published on 2026-07-30. What is real is coverage lag: 1,281 of 1,956 indicator-frequency ids (265,102,798 of 391,910,883 catalog rows, 68%) have not been refreshed since the 2026-06-03 first pass, and logs/_untouched_sweep.txt:118 independently records "ilostat 1,274 of 1,949 file(s) (65%) NOT written since 2026-07-16". The source has had exactly one updater run, is on monthly cadence, and shows ATTENTION/_all:partial in logs/_health_gate.log:37.
- fixable by us: **True**

**Recommended fix, in order:**

> The mislabel is already fixed (664f7b82, on origin/main) — re-run and the message becomes an honest deferral. What still needs doing is the coverage arithmetic, which the fix does not touch: measured throughput was 675 indicators / 25 min ≈ 2.2 s each, so a full sweep of 1,956 needs ~72 min but BUDGET_MIN=25 (ilostat.py:51) buys ~35% of it, and ILO restamps in bulk (350 of the 675 already-published ids went dirty within 4 days), so roughly half of each future budget is consumed re-walking the alphabetical prefix before the tail is reached. Two changes, either of which works: (1) add `run_location: local` to the ilostat registry entry (updater/registry.yaml:2530) so it runs on the workstation, where tools/run_local_heavy.ps1 sets AQUEDUCT_BUDGET_MIN_OVERRIDE and the 25-min cap is lifted (this is exactly why abs/bea were routed local); or (2) raise BUDGET_MIN to ~90 and add load_rotation/save_rotation/rotate_after (updater/strategies/fetchers/_common.py:534-587) so a budget-bounded run does not always restart at the alphabetical top. Do (1) first — it needs no code change and drains the 265M-row backlog in one pass. Separately, ilostat.py:136-138 swallows the exception text (`except Exception: tally.transient_unit(iid)`), so a REAL per-indicator failure here is currently undiagnosable from state.db; record str(e)[:120] with the id.

## 6. Rules that apply to every repair here

- **A key/parser change is a RE-PULL, never a merge** (R22). Changing what `series_key` means leaves the old and new grains coexisting; dedup cannot collapse them because they no longer collide. Use `mode="replace"`, or re-pull the table.
- **Never patch dates — re-pull** (R288). A naive date repair on `cso` would have destroyed 11 of 12 rows; only a negative control caught it. And 41,091 of `stat_slovenia`'s fabricated dates land in 1900–2200, indistinguishable from real data, so no date test can find them.
- **Verify against the store you are actually serving** (R296/R36). Under `AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2` the local directory is a scratch mirror of the last run only; a local check can under-report or give the opposite answer.
- **When a probe reports ABSENCE, run it against something known PRESENT** (R316). An absence looks identical whether the data is missing or the probe is broken.
- **Compare (key, date) pairs, not just keys** (R314). A re-key check that compares identifiers verifies the half you changed on purpose; the half you changed by accident is in the values.
- **A bound over a fixed order is a truncation, not a budget** (R190). If work is capped, check it ROTATES — and specifically that it rotates when the item at the head never completes (R313).
- **Read the job's ARGV, not its progress** (R323). A `--dry-run` and a real run print the same numbers.
